newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil $1.50 to $2 higher, Brent unchanged.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil $1.50 to $2 higher, Brent unchanged.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures were called to open $1.50 to $2.00 a tonne higher on Thursday while Brent was expected to open unchanged, brokers said.

June gas oil closed $2.50 lower on Wednesday at $170.75 a tonne, while June Brent, which expires at the close of business on Thursday, retraced losses in late trade to end just seven cents down at $19.51 a barrel.
"The gas oil is going to catch up with Brent and the arbitrage, there's no other fundamental news," a broker said.
Bearish weekly U.S. stocks data put pressure on the oil complex on Wednesday, but traders expected gas oil to recover in line with Brent and NYMEX futures.
"The market had a fairly strong close last night, it was healthy in the light of the APIs," a broker said.
The June Brent loading programme released on Thursday morning scheduled fewer loadings than the already-thin May programme.
June loadings were set at the equivalent of 38.4 cargoes, including top ups, down from the equivalent of 41.8 cargoes in May.
Traders said the lighter loading programme was due to the shorter month and maintenance at several fields in the Brent system including Bravo, Alwyn, Dunbar and Tern.
